title: Program Acquisition Analyst & Advisor
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Program Acquisition Analyst & Advisor to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
The Program Acquisition Analyst and Advisor provides acquisition analysis, program management insight, and headquarters integration support to Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Fires. The position requires an experienced Army acquisition professional who understands the Fires portfolio and can apply firsthand program management experience to assess program issues, develop recommendations, and support leadership decisions. The successful candidate will have progressive Army acquisition experience culminating in successful completion of a lieutenant colonel–level Centralized Selection List (CSL) acquisition Product Manager assignment. Direct acquisition experience within PEO Missiles and Space, the Rapid Capabilities and Critical Technologies Office (RCCTO), or PAE Fires is required. This is a hands-on analytical and coordination role. The individual develops decision materials, integrates program and staff inputs, tracks priority actions, and helps translate leadership direction into coordinated follow-through. 
Duties: 
Apply Army acquisition and Fires portfolio experience to analyze program execution, identify issues, and develop practical recommendations for leadership consideration.
Assess program cost, schedule, performance, and risk, identifying dependencies and decisions requiring headquarters attention.
Coordinate priority actions across program offices, portfolio elements, and functional staff; consolidate inputs and track actions through completion.
Prepare and refine briefings, decision papers, read-aheads, talking points, and executive correspondence that clearly explain issues, options, and recommended actions.
Support acquisition reviews, program reviews, leadership meetings, and offsites by coordinating materials, identifying decision requirements, and documenting outcomes.
Analyze the relationships among requirements, acquisition strategies, funding, contracting, testing, fielding, and sustainment to identify execution challenges and inform recommendations.
Support resource prioritization and Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) activities by assessing program needs, funding considerations, and portfolio impacts.
Coordinate with Army requirements organizations, acquisition stakeholders, and mission partners to clarify issues and support alignment across organizational boundaries.
Maintain visibility of leadership decisions, taskings, and commitments; identify delays or unresolved issues and coordinate follow-up.
Recommend improvements to acquisition processes, staff coordination, and portfolio governance based on practical program management experience.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
12 plus year of relevant DoD acquisition experience. 
Progressive experience in Army acquisition and program management, including assignments of increasing responsibility leading to CSL selection and service.
Direct acquisition experience within PEO Missiles and Space, RCCTO, or PAE Fires, with demonstrated knowledge of the Fires portfolio.
Substantive responsibility for acquisition program execution and demonstrated understanding of Fires programs, organizational relationships, capability priorities, and acquisition challenges.
Practical knowledge of the Army acquisition process and the Defense Acquisition System, including acquisition strategy development, milestone decisions, requirements integration, contracting, test and evaluation, fielding, and lifecycle sustainment.
Experience managing program cost, schedule, performance, and risk and presenting program status, issues, and recommendations to acquisition leadership.
Working knowledge of PPBE and the relationship between program execution, funding requirements, and resource decisions.
Demonstrated ability to develop clear briefings, decision papers, and written recommendations for senior leaders.
Ability to coordinate across program offices and functional staffs, reconcile competing inputs, and manage multiple actions with established deadlines.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.
Ability to work onsite in Huntsville, Alabama, and travel approximately 10 percent. 
Must have a current driver's license. 
Must be a U.S. Citizen 
Must have an active U.S. DoD Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have a Secret clearance upon hire, and the ability to maintain this clearance level during their employment 
Education Requirements:
Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in engineering, business, management, public administration, or a related field.
Preferred / Desired Skills : 
Recent experience directly supporting or managing Army Fires acquisition programs.
Experience coordinating with acquisition headquarters and preparing materials for General Officer or Senior Executive Service reviews.
DAWIA Program Management certification at the Advanced level or equivalent prior certification.
Master’s degree in engineering, business, management, public administration, national security, military strategy, acquisition, or a related field.
Experience supporting portfolio reviews, cross-program integration, and resource prioritization.
Active Top Secret clearance with Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) eligibility.

title: HUMS Analyst / Programmer
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a HUMS Analyst / Programmer  to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
PeopleTec is seeking an experienced Health and Usage Monitoring System (HUMS) Analyst / Programmer to provide specialized engineering and software development support for the CheckPoint HUMS Test Station.
The position will support the development, modification, integration, troubleshooting, and validation of HUMS test station software and associated hardware interfaces.
This is a temporary, on-call position requiring specialized knowledge of HUMS ground-based systems, software development, data acquisition, and automated testing.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities: 
Support development, maintenance, and enhancement of CheckPoint HUMS Test Station software.
Analyze, modify, debug, and test existing software applications.
Develop and integrate software supporting HUMS data acquisition, processing, and analysis.
Support hardware and software interfaces between HUMS equipment and the test station.
Develop automated test procedures, data simulation, and validation capabilities.
Troubleshoot system communication, instrumentation, and data-processing issues.
Support verification and validation of system functionality and software modifications.
Provide technical documentation and recommendations for system improvements.
Collaborate with engineering personnel to support project-specific development and testing requirements.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
Demonstrated practical experience with HUMS systems, test station software, and hardware integration is essential.
Previous hands-on experience working with CheckPoint HUMS Test Station systems.
Experience developing, maintaining, or troubleshooting HUMS ground-based systems or associated test equipment.
Software development experience using C++, C#, or similar programming languages.
Experience with hardware/software integration, data acquisition, and automated testing.
Working knowledge of aircraft HUMS systems and associated data-processing requirements.
Ability to independently analyze existing software, troubleshoot issues, and implement technical solutions.
Must be a U.S. Citizen
An active DoD Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have an active Secret clearance upon hire, and the ability to maintain this level of clearance during their employment.
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
Desired Skills : 
Experience with military rotorcraft HUMS applications and condition-based maintenance systems.
Familiarity with MIL-STD-1553, ARINC-429, IRIG 106, or similar avionics communication and data interfaces.
Experience with hardware-in-the-loop testing, fault simulation, and automated verification and validation.
Knowledge of vibration analysis, signal processing, and mechanical health monitoring.
Experience with instrumentation, sensor interfaces, and ground support equipment.
Experience with legacy software modification and system modernization.
Employment Conditions : 
This is a temporary, on-call position. Work assignments and hours will be based on project requirements and available funding. No minimum number of work hours is guaranteed.
The employee must be capable of independently performing specialized engineering and software development tasks with minimal supervision.

title: Associate Data Integration & Software Specialist
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking an Associate Data Integration & Software Specialist  to support our Huntsville, AL location.
We are seeking a motivated recent Computer Science graduate to join our technical team as an Associate Data Integration & Software Specialist (Hybrid / On-Site). In this role, you will help design, build, and maintain data exchange pipelines and application interfaces that connect disparate internal databases and external partner platforms.
You will work closely with cross-functional engineering teams, product managers, and external stakeholders to ensure reliable, automated data flow across systems. This position offers an ideal bridge between core software engineering, data architecture, and technical project coordination.
Essential Job Functions 
Data Integration & Interface Development 
Design, build, and maintain data transformation routines and data exchange schemas (e.g., XML, JSON, REST APIs) to enable seamless communication between heterogeneous software platforms.
Implement parsers, validation routines, and automated import/export pipelines to ensure clean data migration and interoperability across systems.
Modernize legacy data structures and formats by converting them into standardized, scalable web and enterprise schema standards.
Conduct initial testing, debugging, and quality verification on data exchange workflows prior to deployment.
Technical Coordination & Project Support 
Coordinate cross-functional technical syncs and sprint reviews; assist in establishing sprint milestones and tracking team deliverables.
Document meeting notes, track action items, and follow up with internal development teams and external partners on technical requirements and open tickets.
Monitor project deadlines and proactively communicate roadblocks or timeline risks to technical leads and management.
Collaborate with senior engineers to evaluate potential vendor proposals, software tools, or third-party APIs for system compatibility and performance.
Documentation & Technical Communication 
Draft comprehensive system interface documentation, API specifications, data flow diagrams, and user guides.
Present technical updates, data metrics, and project status briefings to team leads, non-technical stakeholders, and peers.
Prepare clear technical write-ups proposing solutions or corrective actions for data pipeline bottlenecks.
General Team Responsibilities 
Collaborate with fellow developers, systems analysts, and operations personnel to support continuous integration and operational reliability.
Perform code reviews, adhere to standard version control practices, and follow team software development lifecycle (SDLC) standards.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
0-2 years of experience
Core Technical Knowledge: Strong foundational understanding of data structures, algorithms, relational/non-relational databases, and client-server architectures.
Data Interchange & Scripting: Hands-on experience (via coursework, academic projects, or internships) working with structured data formats (XML, JSON, CSV), schema validation (XSD, JSON Schema), and at least one programming/scripting language (e.g., Python, Java, C#, or JavaScript/Node.js).
Database Fundamentals: Proficiency with SQL and querying relational databases (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server).
Communication & Collaboration: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to document code clearly and present technical concepts to peers and project leads.
Tools: Familiarity with modern collaboration suites (Microsoft Office 365, Teams, Slack) and version control platforms (Git/GitHub/GitLab).
Ability to travel up to 15–20% for on-site team planning or stakeholder workshops as required.
Must be a U.S. Citizen
An active DoD Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have an active Secret clearance upon hire, and the ability to maintain this level of clearance during their employment.
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Information Systems, or a closely related technical field (graduated within the last 12 months or nearing graduation).
Preferred: 
Exposure to RESTful API design, web services, or middleware/integration platforms.
Experience with ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines or messaging queues.
Prior internship, capstone project, or open-source contribution involving cross-system data transfer or interface design.
Basic understanding of project management methodologies (Agile/Scrum, Jira, Trello).

title: Mid-to-Senior-Level Engineer/Analyst
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Mid-to-Senior-Level Engineer/Analyst to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
PeopleTec is seeking a Systems Engineer/Analyst to support Missile Defense Agency Systems Engineering Directorate to provide Verification and Validation support for the System Verification Director . This position plays a key role in defining, analyzing, and managing requirements spanning the entire system life cycle - from concept development through testing and deployment.
Duties: 
Develop/maintain code for Ground Test and Flight Test data analysis required by MDA/SEQV. Coordinate with other developers collaborating on code modifications and analysis tools within a code repository of thousands of executable lines of python code housed in a git repository environment.
Write Python, MATLAB, and shell command scripts to verify and validate test system requirements for Missile Defense Elements using Ground Test and Flight Test data.
Execute System Interface Control Document (SICD) requirements checkout using MATLAB requirements analysis code against tactical message log data recorded from flight and ground test data sources.
Develop scripts to import, parse, and extract Missile Defense Data Center (MDDC) ground test and flight test data to be used for MDA/SEQV activities including Threat V&V analysis, Core Truth Model (CTM) analysis, SICD analysis, and System Federation Validation Events (SFVE) / System Post Flight Reconstruction (SPFR) performance parameter analysis.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
5-8+ years of relevant experience.
Proven experience in systems engineering supporting missile defense or other complex defense systems.
Must have a strong ability to use Python, MATLAB , and ability to execute operating system shell command scripts 
Strong understanding of MDA system architectures , lifecycle processes, and verification/validation. 
Ability to translate high-level mission objectives into detailed technical requirements.
Excellent analytical, documentation, and communication skills.
Must be a U.S. Citizen.
An active DoD  Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have an active  Secret  clearance upon hire, and the ability to maintain this level of clearance during their employment.  
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or related technical field (or equivalent combination of education and experience)

title: Mid-to-Senior-Level Engineer/Analyst
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Mid-to-Senior-Level Engineer/Analyst to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
We are seeking a motivated engineer/analyst to provide Modeling and Simulation (M&S) Verification, Validation, and Accreditation (VV&A) support to the Missile Defense Agency (MDA) System Verification directorate. The selected candidate will serve a lead role for M&S accreditation efforts associated with Aegis BMD, Sensor (e.g., Cobra Dane, UEWR, AN/TPY-2, SBX, LRDR), or other models represented in the MDA Ground Test (GT) events. 
This is a full-time, on-site position at a government customer location. The selected candidate will collaborate with Government customers, internal and external Missile Defense Agency (MDA) stakeholders, program offices, and M&S development prime contractors.
Duties: 
Serve as subject matter expert for information (e.g., M&S versions, V&V plans, M&S versus tactical boundaries) associated with assigned Hardware-in-the-Loop (HWIL) M&S.
Coordinate with model owners to develop executable action plans to ensure timely delivery of V&V evidence supporting accreditation information needs for MDA M&S accreditation assessments of applicable GT data sources.
Conduct technical review of V&V evidence and develop M&S accreditation recommendations for the MDA accreditation authority.
Author sections and/or provide technical input for relevant products such as the MDA M&S accreditation report/briefing, MDA M&S accreditation decision memorandum, and MDA M&S accreditation plan.
Develop Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&M) to address high-priority issues affecting M&S accreditation.
Regularly interface with the model owner and V&V agent to address M&S limitations impacting accreditation outcomes. Document and maintain M&S limitation resolution plans in a dedicated online repository for tracking and reporting purposes.
Collaborate with model owners to maintain or refine Performance Parameters, Acceptability Criteria, and Evaluation Methodologies for inclusion in current and future releases of the M&S Accreditation Plan.
Support Operational Capability List (OCL) Working Group (OWG) meetings to brief MDA M&S accreditation status for HWIL models supporting Missile Defense System (MDS) performance assessment of capabilities to be fielded.
Provide regular verbal and written status updates to leadership regarding M&S VV&A areas of responsibility.
Perform other related tasks as assigned by the Director, MDA System Verification or M&S VV&A lead and strategic advisor.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
5-8+ years of relevant experience.
Proven experience with modeling and simulation applications.
Knowledge of M&S VV&A principles, methodologies, and accreditation processes.
Experience evaluating technical evidence of complex defense systems, and developing defensible engineering recommendations.
Familiarity with the Missile Defense System architecture and its integrated defense systems.
Ability to independently lead technical assessments, work within a multi-disciplinary team, develop action plans, and communicate status and findings to government leadership.
Strong technical writing, analytical, problem-solving, communication, and presentation skills.
Must be a U.S. Citizen.
An active DoD  Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have an active  Secret  clearance upon hire, and the ability to maintain this level of clearance during their employment.  
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, or related technical discipline.
Desired Skills : 
Top Secret clearance preferred.
Advanced degree in Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
Demonstrated experience with the Aegis BMD weapon system and/or Sensor components of the Missile Defense System architecture.
Experience developing or reviewing M&S accreditation plans, V&V reports, accreditation assessments, and technical recommendations.

title: Program Integrator
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Program Integrator  to support our Huntsville, AL location.
The Program Integrator supporting Advanced C-UAS Effects (ACE) Project Office ensures seamless integration across functional areas within the Product Office and synchronizes activities with supporting Project Management (PM) and Product Management (PdM) Offices, as well as external organizations. This role manages highly complex integration efforts spanning multiple technical disciplines, logistics concepts, and system‑of‑systems interfaces. The Program Integrator coordinates Government matrixed support and contractor teams to define interoperability requirements, align program tasks, and evaluate progress against program plans. The position supports senior leaders through analysis, planning, and decision‑quality products; facilitates cross‑organizational collaboration; identifies and mitigates programmatic and technical risks; and ensures effective implementation of program direction across all concurrent technical efforts.
Duties: 
Program Integration - Coordinate and integrate technical, programmatic, and logistics activities across PM ACE, supporting PM/PdM offices, and external organizations to ensure alignment with program objectives.

PeopleTec is currently seeking a Mid-Level Exportability Engineer  to support our Huntsville, AL location.
The candidate will serve as a Mid-Level Exportability Engineer within a Project Management Office (PMO) within PAE Fires and will be responsible for providing technical support to the program's Chief Engineer and the Product Manager. The candidate will be responsible for the technical suitability, feasibility, and requirements analysis for integrating exportability features into advanced defense systems. The candidate will bridge system architecture with Technology Security and Foreign Disclosure (TSFD) policy, performing the engineering assessments required to protect U.S. technologies (Anti-Tamper) while defining viable configurations for allied partners, and will provide technical expertise to help stand up, scope, and evaluate new DEF studies for future programs entering the exportability pipeline. The candidate will prepare and present exportability engineering findings, reports, and improvement plans to senior management and stakeholders. Provide technical support and leadership in exportability engineering across the system lifecycle (design, development, acquisition, integration, testing, fielding, and sustainment). 
Conduct comprehensive audits of baseline system architectures to identify Critical Program Information (CPI), advanced algorithms, and cutting-edge hardware susceptible to reverse engineering. 
Assist in standing up additional DEF studies by conducting preliminary technical evaluations, defining initial engineering task scope, and estimating the technical feasibility of export modifications for new weapon systems. 
Investigate and define high-level conceptual approaches for protecting sensitive technologies, including strategies for system modularity that allow hardware substitution or software modulation in export variants. 
Architect conceptual export variants based on TSFD assessments, and evaluate these variants to ensure they meet required performance metrics while satisfying U.S. export security criteria. 
Use modeling and simulation to assess how proposed DEF modifications, such as altered guidance code or added AT hardware, will impact a system's baseline kinematic performance, weight, and operational lethality. 
Draft validated CPI and Critical Component Matrices and High-Level AT and Modularity Strategies, and support the technical drafting of formal foreign release documentation, such as Exception to the National Disclosure Policy (ENDP) Position Papers. 
Ensure compliance with defense and industry standards by managing exportability engineering processes effectively. 
Interface with internal teams and external organizations to coordinate exportability engineering objectives and strategies. 
Prepare and present exportability engineering findings, reports, and improvement plans to senior management and stakeholders. 
Conduct strategic planning and coordination to support program objectives.

Use digital tools and methodologies to manage cost, schedule, and performance for assigned activities. 
Perform other tasks as assigned by the Chief Engineer and/or Product Manager.

5+ years of relevant experience. Additional education may be substituted for years of experience. 
Demonstrated experience in exportability engineering, particularly within defense or aerospace industries. 
Working knowledge of Anti-Tamper (AT) principles, reverse engineering mitigation, and Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA). 
Experience with complex weapon systems, Counter-UAS (C-UAS) architectures, or advanced sensor/seeker integration. 
Proficiency with modeling and simulation tools used to assess kinematics and system performance impacts.

title: Interoperability Systems Engineer
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking an Interoperability Systems Engineer  to support our Huntsville, AL location.
The candidate will serve as an Interoperability Systems Engineer within a Project Management Office (PMO) within PAE Fires and will be responsible for providing technical support to the program's Chief Engineer and the Product Manager. The candidate will define, manage, and govern the open system architecture that enables the seamless and timely integration of new sensors, effectors, and C2/Fire Control support systems into the IBCS architecture across the system lifecycle (design, development, acquisition, integration, testing, fielding, and sustainment). The candidate will prepare and present interoperability findings, reports, and improvement plans to senior management and stakeholders. Will work within and/or lead a multidisciplinary team to achieve program goals. Perform other tasks as assigned by the Chief Engineer and/or Product Manager.
The candidate will be required to interface with internal PMs across PAE Fires and external organizations to include HQDA, ASA(ALT), JIATF 401, ATEC, AMCOM, and others for coordination and synchronization of interoperability technical and programmatic objectives.
Duties: 
Provide technical support and leadership in interoperability across the system lifecycle (design, development, acquisition, integration, testing, fielding, and sustainment). 
Implement a single pane of glass, enabling one fire control system to manage many sensors and effectors. 
Ensure developer APIs and SDKs for third-party sensor/effector vendor integration are specified, delivered, and validated. 
Define and oversee the Glueware interfaces needed to support open systems and prevent Government vendor lock. 
Review and approve Open API and SDK implementation documentation. 
Establish an open standards policy that prevents vendor lock and provides the ability to integrate with agnostic fire control and C2 systems. 
Ensure compliance with defense and industry standards by managing interoperability processes effectively. 
Interface with internal teams and external organizations to coordinate interoperability objectives and strategies. 
Prepare and present interoperability findings, reports, and improvement plans to senior management and stakeholders. 
Conduct strategic planning and coordination to support program objectives. 
Provide technical guidance and leadership to peer and subordinate engineers within the interoperability team. 
Use digital tools and methodologies to manage cost, schedule, and performance for assigned activities. 
Perform other tasks as assigned by the Chief Engineer and/or Product Manager.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
5+ years of relevant experience. Additional education may be substituted for years of experience. 
Demonstrated experience in interoperability, particularly within defense or aerospace industries. 
Knowledge of developing and managing open systems architectures. 
Strong knowledge of industry standards and defense requirements. 
Excellent communication and presentation skills. 
Ability to lead and work within a multidisciplinary team. 
Previous experience working in a U.S. Government Program Office (required). 
Travel: 25%
Must be a U.S. Citizen
An active DoD Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have an active Secret clearance upon hire, and the ability to maintain this level of clearance during their employment.
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor's degree in Engineering (or related technical discipline). 
Desired Skills : 
Top Secret clearance preferred

Knowledge of DoD Directive 5200.47E (Anti-Tamper), DoDI 5200.44 (Trusted Systems/SCRM), NIST SP 800-161, Cryptographic Key Zeroization/Encapsulation, Secure Boot/TrustZone, FPGA/ASIC Bitstream Protection, and IDEA-STD-1010.

Required Skills/Experience :

title: Business and Financial Analyst
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Business and Financial Analyst to support our Huntsville, AL location.
We are seeking a Business and Financial Analyst to support the Army’s Portfolio Acquisition Executive Fires Office (PAE Fires). This role involves leading budget formulation, execution, and reporting activities to ensure the effective allocation and utilization of resources in support of mission objectives. The Budget Analyst will collaborate with program managers, contracting officers, and other stakeholders to ensure compliance with Department of Defense (DoD) financial regulations and policies. This is a fast-paced role requiring strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills.
Duties: 
Develop, prepare, and manage program budgets, including Program Objective Memorandum (POM) submissions, spend plans, and obligation/expenditure forecasts.
Coordinate and execute funding actions, including drafting and submitting Purchase Requisitions (PRs), Military Interdepartmental Purchase Requests (MIPRs), and Direct Charge (DC) transactions.
Monitor and track the execution of funds to ensure alignment with program goals and timelines.
Conduct detailed financial analyses to identify trends, variances, and risks.
Prepare and present financial reports, briefings, and recommendations to leadership and stakeholders.
Maintain historical financial records and update funding history tracking when funds are received.
Monitor contract status, including ceiling limits, periods of performance, and funding requirements.
Support Contracting Officer Representatives (CORs) by analyzing monthly contractor reports, facilitating communication, and supporting  documentation for contract actions (e.g. Technical Directives (TDs) and Requests for Services Contract Approval (RSCAs).
Participate in Contract Integrated Product Teams (IPTs), Program Management Reviews (PMRs), and financial/metrics meetings.
Ensure compliance with DoD financial management regulations, policies, and procedures.
Facilitate fiscal year-end close to ensure 100% obligation of expiring funds.
Support audits and reviews by providing accurate and timely financial data.
Coordinate with program managers and technical leads to align financial plans with program objectives.
Facilitate financial communication and coordination between the Project Office, higher headquarters, and external customers.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
Minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in budget analysis, financial management, or related roles, preferably within the DoD or federal government.
Demonstrated experience with DoD financial systems, including General Fund Enterprise Business System (GFEBS).
Experience preparing and submitting PRs, MIPRs, and DC transactions.
Proven ability to monitor funds execution and create financial reports.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including advanced Excel functions (e.g., pivot tables, VLOOKUP, and data visualization).
Familiarity with financial management tools and software used in DoD environments.
Strong understanding of DoD financial regulations, including the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and DoD Financial Management Regulation (FMR).
Knowledge of appropriations, funding types, and fiscal law principles.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex financial data to diverse audiences.
Ability to manage diverse workloads of complex and priority projects without supervision.
Strong leadership, analytical, and organizational skills.
Must have a current driver's license. 
Travel: 20% 
Must be a U.S. Citizen 
Active U.S. DoD Secret clearance is required to perform this work. 
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.
Master’s degree preferred.
Desired Skills : 
10+ years of relevant experience in financial management, budget analysis, or related roles within the DoD.
Certification in financial management or related areas (e.g., Certified Defense Financial Manager (CDFM), DoD Financial Management Certification).
Familiarity with rapid acquisition or prototyping programs and their unique financial requirements.
In-depth understanding of the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) process.
Ability to provide guidance and informal mentoring to junior analysts, as required.
Ability to identify and implement innovative solutions to improve financial processes and program outcomes.
Experience using data visualization and advanced analytics tools.

Torch Technologies Inc., is seeking a Mid-Level Software Engineer. In this position, the candidate will be part of a dynamic team responsible for integrating vendor-developed flight software into a proprietary 6-degree-of-freedom (6DOF) simulation environment to support independent verification and validation (IV&V) of flight software for the Missile Defense Agency (MDA) Targets and Countermeasures program. This role focuses on the software integration layer connecting external vendor flight code to an in-house 6DOF simulation framework, ensuring accurate interface behavior, timing, data exchange, and functional compliance prior to and during test execution.

Debugging integration issues arising from differences in vendor coding practices, compilers, data structures, and timing assumptions versus the host simulation.
Supporting IV&V test execution by configuring simulation scenarios, verifying flight software behavior against expected 6DOF trajectory and dynamics outputs, and documenting discrepancies.
Working closely with simulation architects, systems engineers, and vendor points of contact to troubleshoot integration failures and validate fixes.
Publishing integration status reports, test readiness documentation, and briefing materials summarizing analysis results.

US Citizenship.

About the Job
CFD Research is excited to invite applications for a full-time Maintainability and Testability Engineer! In this role, you'll play a key part in supporting the continued growth, production, and lifecycle management of a complex multidisciplinary aerospace and defense hardware system.
Your mission will be to develop and enhance the engineering framework that ensures our system can effectively detect and isolate failures, support troubleshooting, provide vital diagnostic information, facilitate efficient maintenance, and be ready for service after maintenance activities.
You’ll have the opportunity to collaborate closely with a diverse team, including reliability experts, systems engineers, design engineers, controls and software professionals, test engineers, manufacturing teams, product support staff, maintainers, technicians, and program leaders.
About the Role
As the Maintainability and Testability Engineer, you’ll evaluate the system from the perspective of the personnel who maintain and support it throughout its lifecycle. Your insights will translate known and predicted system failure behaviors into practical requirements and strategies for fault detection, fault isolation, built-in testing, diagnostics, accessibility, maintenance, repair, support equipment, and verification.
This position offers significant involvement in design maturation, where you’ll leverage information from FMEA and FMECA, testing, maintenance activities, and real-world failure experiences to identify opportunities for enhancing system maintainability and testability.
What You’ll Do
Develop and maintain the system maintainability and testability engineering framework.
Develop and maintain Maintenance Task Analyses.
Perform or support Level of Repair Analysis.
Develop fault detection and fault isolation analyses.
Define expected fault-isolation capability and diagnostic resolution.
Develop and maintain integrated diagnostics and testability analyses.
Evaluate Built-In-Test capabilities, diagnostic coverage, limitations, and failure-detection performance.
Collaborate with controls, software, electrical, mechanical, and other engineering teams to enhance BIT and diagnostic functionality.
Assess health-monitoring and prognostic capabilities where applicable.
Work alongside the Systems Reliability Engineer to ensure significant failure modes identified through FMEA and FMECA are appropriately detectable and isolatable.
Evaluate accessibility, removal and replacement activities, maintenance sequences, maintenance times, tooling, personnel requirements, and support-equipment needs.
Identify maintainability-related design deficiencies and collaborate with responsible design organizations to develop corrective actions.
Support Reliability Centered Maintenance activities and the development of maintenance tasks and intervals.
Assist in repair-versus-replace decisions and other repair-level analyses.
Develop the engineering basis for maintenance and repair procedures and support the development of technical publications.
Review maintenance manuals, troubleshooting procedures, and related technical content for consistency with the system design and diagnostic strategy.
Identify and evaluate support-equipment requirements associated with system maintenance, troubleshooting, and diagnostics.
Support Human Systems Integration activities affecting system operation and maintenance.
Develop or support maintainability, BIT, diagnostics, fault-isolation, and human-engineering demonstrations.
Define verification approaches and evidence required to demonstrate compliance with maintainability and testability requirements.
Collaborate with the Systems Test Engineer to develop and execute formal maintainability, BIT, diagnostics, and fault-isolation verification activities.
Evaluate actual maintenance, test, and failure data to refine maintainability assumptions and diagnostic strategies.
Support product-support and lifecycle engineering activities requiring maintainability or testability expertise.
Basic Qualifications: 
Bachelor’s degree in systems engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, aerospace engineering, industrial engineering, or another closely related engineering discipline.
Three or more years of relevant engineering experience involving maintainability, testability, diagnostics, maintenance engineering, product support, hardware integration, testing, or a related technical area.
Understanding of hardware failure modes and the relationship between failure behavior, fault detection, fault isolation, troubleshooting, and repair.
Ability to understand technical drawings, system architecture, controls logic, maintenance information, test results, and engineering requirements.
Strong technical writing and analytical skills.
Ability to work directly with engineers, technicians, maintainers, test personnel, and product-support personnel.
U.S. citizenship required due to the nature of the company's work and contractual requirements.
Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance, as required.
Desired Qualifications: 
Experience developing Maintenance Task Analyses, Level of Repair Analysis, Reliability Centered Maintenance, or related maintenance engineering products.
Experience with Built-In-Test, integrated diagnostics, fault detection, fault isolation, or testability analysis.
Experience with FMEA or FMECA and translating failure modes into diagnostic or maintenance requirements.
Experience developing or evaluating maintainability demonstrations.
Experience working directly with maintainers or technicians on complex aerospace, defense, industrial, or electromechanical hardware.
Experience with technical publications, troubleshooting procedures, support equipment, or product-support analysis.
Experience supporting DoD acquisition, qualification, production, or lifecycle sustainment programs.

Job Description: 
The Rotorcraft Flight Dynamics Modeling and Simulation Engineer will support Army rotorcraft engineering efforts through the development, improvement, and application of flight-dynamics models for both legacy fleet and future vertical lift, including models needed for real-time piloted simulations.  Additionally, the position will support the development of flight-dynamics models for simulation of advanced and novel vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) aircraft configurations, both manned and unmanned.
Advanced flight-dynamics modeling and analysis tools such as Gen Hel, FORECAST, and HeliUM are used to predict the responses of Army rotorcraft under various configurations and flight conditions, including real-time simulation with a pilot in the loop. They are also used to generate high-order linear models that are needed to design and optimize both flight controls and autonomy algorithms for Army rotorcraft.
Responsibilities

Develop proficiency with the HeliUM comprehensive modeling tool.  Update HeliUM as need to generate reduced-order real-time aerodynamics simulation models for UAS.
Develop and validate UH-60M flight dynamics simulation models to enhance existing capabilities by enabling the modeling and simulation of relevant rotorcraft configurations.  Assess and plan the necessary source code modifications and investigate considerations for the software development environment.
Conduct applied research to develop and validate advanced identification techniques needed to accurately model configurations with multiple redundant effectors.  Validate and update models so that they can in-turn be used to more accurately predict further configuration changes.
Attend technical group meetings, branch meetings, design reviews, etc. and report project updates and activities.
Communicate research results through technical presentations and written reports.

About the Job
CFD Research is seeking a full-time Systems Reliability Engineer to support the continued maturation, verification, and production of a complex multidisciplinary aerospace and defense hardware system.
The Systems Reliability Engineer will maintain and mature the program reliability engineering framework and will work closely with design engineering, systems engineering, test, manufacturing, quality, maintainability and testability, product support, and program leadership.
The position will be responsible for maintaining the quantitative reliability prediction model in Windchill as well as developing and maintaining FMEA and FMECA, reliability allocations, failure analyses, reliability fault trees, FRACAS analytics, reliability-growth assessments, and critical-item evaluations.
About the Role
The Systems Reliability Engineer will be responsible for understanding how the system can fail, how often failures are expected to occur, which failure modes dominate system reliability, and whether design and corrective actions are improving the system as intended.
The reliability prediction model, FMEA and FMECA, failure analyses, and FRACAS information will be maintained as living engineering products and updated as the system design changes, component selections mature, verification testing generates new information, failures occur, and corrective actions are implemented.
The engineer will also provide reliability inputs to the assigned System Safety owner, including relevant failure modes, failure rates, fault logic, criticality information, and corrective-action status when those inputs are needed to maintain system hazard analyses or safety assessments.
What You’ll Do
Develop, maintain, and mature the system reliability prediction model using Windchill.
Maintain consistency between the reliability prediction model, current system configuration, component and assembly information, and applicable reliability assumptions.
Update reliability predictions as designs mature, parts change, operating assumptions change, failure data become available, or corrective actions modify the system configuration.
Develop and maintain reliability allocations and predictions at appropriate system, subsystem, assembly, and component levels.
Evaluate predicted reliability against system requirements and identify significant reliability drivers, contributors, and areas of insufficient margin.
Work with design engineering and other technical organizations to obtain component data, operating conditions, duty cycles, environmental assumptions, and failure information required to maintain the reliability model.
Develop, maintain, and mature system-level FMEA and FMECA analyses.
Coordinate subsystem and component failure-mode information with responsible engineering organizations.
Maintain failure severity, criticality, consequence, and related analytical information as the design and operating knowledge mature.
Develop and maintain reliability fault-tree analyses where appropriate.
Analyze test, manufacturing, and operational failure information for trends, recurring failure mechanisms, and emerging reliability risks.
Support and maintain the technical analysis portion of the program FRACAS process.
Work with responsible engineering organizations to investigate failures, identify root causes, establish corrective actions, and evaluate corrective-action effectiveness.
Use actual test, manufacturing, and operational failure information to assess and refine reliability-model assumptions where appropriate.
Evaluate the reliability impact of engineering changes and proposed corrective actions.
Maintain traceability between reliability predictions, FMEA and FMECA results, critical-item assessments, FRACAS information, and the current technical baseline.
Identify reliability-critical items using applicable failure analyses, reliability predictions, design information, operational information, and program criteria.
Generate reliability-model results and supporting analyses for technical reviews, customer deliverables, design trades, and verification activities.
Work with the Maintainability and Testability Engineer to ensure significant failure modes are appropriately detectable, isolatable, and maintainable.
Work with the Verification, Compliance and MBSE Systems Engineer to identify and trace verification evidence needed to support reliability requirements and analytical conclusions.
Provide reliability data and analyses to the assigned System Safety owner where reliability information supports hazard analysis, safety assessment, or safety-critical item decisions.

Bachelor’s degree in reliability engineering, systems engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, aerospace engineering, chemical engineering, or another relevant technical discipline.
Three or more years of experience involving reliability engineering, failure analysis, hardware development, or a closely related engineering activity.
Experience developing, maintaining, or interpreting quantitative reliability prediction models for complex hardware systems.
Experience developing, maintaining, or using FMEA, FMECA, fault-tree analysis, or similar reliability engineering products.
Ability to work with component-level reliability information, system configurations, operating environments, duty cycles, failure-rate data, and engineering assumptions to maintain a defensible system reliability prediction.
Ability to understand multidisciplinary hardware systems and evaluate failure propagation and consequence.
Experience investigating technical failures and working with design engineers to establish root cause and corrective action.
Strong technical writing and analytical communication skills.
Ability to translate analytical findings into practical engineering actions and verification needs.
U.S. citizenship required due to the nature of the company's work and contractual requirements.
Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance, as required.

Experience using Windchill for reliability prediction, reliability analysis, or related reliability and maintainability activities.
Experience maintaining reliability models through design maturation, configuration changes, testing, production, and corrective-action implementation.

location: Redstone Arsenal, Alabama; Rock Island, Illinois; Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland; Fort Detrick, Maryland; Fort Meade, Maryland; Prince George's County, Maryland; Silver Spring, Maryland; Picatinny Arsenal, New Jersey; Charlottesville County, Virginia; Fort AP Hill, Virginia; Fort Belvoir, Virginia; Fort Myer, Virginia
text:
This is a Direct Hire Authority (DHA) solicitation utilizing the DHA for Certain Personnel of the DoD Workforce to recruit and appoint qualified candidates to positions in the competitive service. About the Position: The U.S. Army Installation Management Command (IMCOM) handles the day-to-day operations of Army installations.
Qualifications: ****This is an open continuous announcement. We accept applications on an ongoing basis. Applications will be reviewed bi-weekly and referred for selection as vacancies occur within the organization.**** Recruitment and relocation incentives may be authorized. Salary negotiations for those candidates who are new to Federal service or have a break in service may be authorized. Credit for prior non-Federal work experience and certain military service for determining annual leave accrual rate may be authorized. Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. For GS-5: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: 1) Experience applying a body of basic laws and regulations; 2) Assisting with law enforcement operations practices and/or techniques; and 3) Maintaining order and protecting life and property. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-04). (Note: Successful completion of a Federal, State, county, or municipal police academy or comparable training course which included at least 40 classroom hours of instruction in police department procedures and methods, and local law and regulations, may be substituted for three months of specialized experience.) OR Education: Four years of education above the high school level in an accredited school leading to a bachelor's degree in Police Science or a comparable degree program related to the work of the position, such as Criminal Justice. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide your semester hours of education by 120. Add the two percentages. For GS-6: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: 1) Maintaining order and protecting life; 2) Responding to citizens in emergency/non-emergency situations; and 3) Protecting property against such hazards as fire, theft, damage, accident, or trespass. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-05). Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone -- no substitution of education for experience is permitted. For GS-7: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: 1) Performing law enforcement investigation in accordance with established policies and procedures; 2) Collecting/preserving evidence for an investigation; and 3) Preparing statements concerning incidents such as accidents or law violations. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-06). Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone -- no substitution of education for experience is permitted. Creditable specialized experience may have been gained in work on a police force; through service as a military police officer; in work providing visitor protection and law enforcement in parks, forests, or other natural resource or recreational environments; in performing criminal investigative duties; or in other work that provided the required knowledge and skills.
Education: FOREIGN EDUCATION: If you are using education completed in foreign colleges or universities to meet the qualification requirements, you must show the education credentials have been evaluated by a private organization that specializes in interpretation of foreign education programs and such education has been deemed equivalent to that gained in an accredited U.S. education program; or full credit has been given for the courses at a U.S. accredited college or university. For further information, visit: https://sites.ed.gov/international/recognition-of-foreign-qualifications/
Requirements: 
Exercise exclusive law enforcement jurisdiction responsible for the, apprehension or detention of persons suspected or convicted of offenses against the criminal laws of the United States.
Serve as a police patrol officer enforcing Federal criminal laws and the Uniform Code of Military Justice (UCMJ) involving persons and property.
Protect government property, materials and facilities against trespass, theft, fire, damage and espionage.
Detain or arrest suspected or guilty persons.
Collect and protect evidence, witnesses, victims, etc.
Arrest persons committing or suspected of committing crimes on the installation.
Patrol assigned area by vehicle or on foot to preserve the peace, prevent crime, and protect lives and property.
Security clearance: Secret.

title: Program Analyst  (Space Operations)
location: Redstone Arsenal, Alabama; Schriever AFB, Colorado; Offutt AFB, Nebraska
text:
Click on "Learn more about this agency" button below for IMPORTANT additional information. The primary purpose of this position is to perform a variety of duties in the analysis and evaluation of cyber operations, and to complete developmental assignments and training outlined in the formal training and development plan.
Qualifications: Any individual who was awarded a degree by an institution of higher education from a PUBLIC or other non-profit institution not more than two years before the date of appointment meets the basic eligibility requirement to apply for the DHA Recent Graduates Program; OR Any individual who has completed a period of obligated service in a uniformed service of more than four years and was awarded a degree by an institution of higher education from a public or other non-profit institution not more than four years before the closing of this announcement meets the basic eligibility requirement to apply for the DHA Recent Graduates Program. You must have completed a 4 year course of study leading to a bachelor's from an accredited institution AND must have documented Superior Academic Achievement (SAA) at the undergraduate level in one of the following: a) Class Standing - upper third of the graduating class based on completed courses in the college, university, or major subdivision; b) Grade Point Average - 2.95 or higher out of a possible 4.0 as recorded on your official transcript or as computed based on 4 years of education or as computed based on courses completed during the final 2 years of curriculum; OR 3.45 or higher out of a possible 4.0 based on the average of the required courses completed in your major field or the required courses in your major field completed during the final 2 years of your curriculum. If more than 10 percent of total undergraduate credit hours are non-graded, i.e. pass/fail, CLEP, CCAF, DANTES, military credit, etc, you cannot qualify based on GPA; c) Election to membership in a national scholastic honor society (note: freshman honor society cannot be used to meet the requirements of this position). (If qualifying based on class standing or honor society membership, provide appropriate documentation). Qualified candidates will be considered in accordance with the Office of Personnel Management Pathways Guidelines . You can also visit: http://www.opm.gov/qualifications/standards/index-Standards.asp for additional qualification standards. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. ***PLEASE NOTE***This position requires the ability to obtain/maintain a Top Secret clearance level As a condition of employment for accepting this position, you will be required to serve a 1-year probationary period OR 2-year trial period during which we will evaluate your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest. In determining if your employment advances the public interest, we may consider: - your performance and conduct; - the needs and interests of the agency; - whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency of the Government; and - whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency if the Federal service. Upon completion of your probationary period OR trial period, your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest.
Education: The PALACE Acquire Program offers you a permanent position upon completion of your formal training plan. As a PALACE Acquire Intern you will experience both personal and professional growth while dealing effectively and ethically with change, complexity, and problem solving. The program offers a 2 or 3 year formal training plan with eligibility for yearly salary increases. Promotions and salary increases are based upon your successful performance and supervisory approval. This is your opportunity to begin a successful civilian career with the United States Air Force.This position has an education requirement. You MUST provide transcripts to support your educational claims. Education must be accredited by an accrediting institution recognized by the U.S. Department of Education. http://www2.ed.gov/admins/finaid/accred/index.htmlPlease submit copies of all transcripts, to include transferred hours-official copies are not required at time of application. If selected, you will be required to provide official copies of all transcripts. NOTE: Degree Audits are not accepted. If you qualify based on undergraduate, or higher level education, and you have not graduated prior to applying for this position, you may be offered a position, contingent upon your final grade point average or class ranking. FOREIGN EDUCATION: Education completed in foreign colleges or universities may be used to meet the requirements. You must show proof the education credentials have been deemed to be at least equivalent to that gained in conventional U.S. education program. It is your responsibility to provide such evidence when applying.
Requirements: 
Performs moderately difficult and complex assignments consisting of well precedented tasks to further orient the employee in the application of occupational and agency missions, policies, and objectives, as well as tactics, techniques, procedures. Incumbent determines the practices and procedures to use in accomplishing conventional tasks, and interprets and adapts guidelines in order to resolve procedural or factual issues. Carries out special projects and participates in special initiatives and studies. Prepare oral and written correspondence and other documentation.
Security clearance: Top Secret.

company: United States Army Installation Management Command (federal)
title: Food and Beverage Attendant (Snack Bar) NA-02
text:
This position is located at Redstone Arsenal, Alabama. Incentives and Bonuses Incentives will not be paid.
Qualifications: Resumes must be two pages (or less). Resumes should clearly demonstrate the applicant's relevant experience, skills, knowledge and abilities as they pertain to this position. A qualified candidate must possess the following: Must meet state/local age requirements at the time of appointment if serving alcoholic beverages. title: SURFACE MAINTENANCE REPAIRER (T32)
text:
THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. This National Guard position is for a SURFACE MAINTENANCE REPAIRER (T32), Position Description Number D1193000 and is part of the AL UTES 3, National Guard. ORGANIZATION: AL UTES 3, HUNTSVILLE, AL SELECTING OFFICIAL: CW4 F. PEPPER
Qualifications: MILITARY REQUIREMENTS: This is an excepted service position that requires membership in a compatible military grade in the Alabama Army National Guard. Applicants who are not currently a member of the Alabama Army National Guard must be eligible for immediate membership. If you are not sure you are eligible for military membership, please contact an Alabama Army National Guard recruiter at 800-464-8273 prior to applying for this position. MINIMUM MILITARY RANK: PVT MAXIMUM MILITARY RANK: SFC EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS: Each applicant must fully substantiate (in his/her own words) that he/she meets the requirements of the Specialized Experience listed below: Otherwise, the applicant will be considered unqualified for this position. DO NOT COPY THE VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT OR THE POSITION DESCRIPTION. DOING SO MAY RESULT IN DISQUALIFICATION FOR THE POSITION. GENERAL EXPERIENCE: Experience or training which demonstrates knowledge of equipment to be able to do routine jobs, simple preventative maintenance tasks, and can use common tools and equipment in the line of work. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Experience or training using common hand and power tools and a small variety of test and measurement devices to make mechanical repairs. Experience removing, adjusting, replacing, cleaning, and installing a variety of parts, components, and accessories. Experience which demonstrates a basic understanding of mechanical, electrical, and hydraulic theory applying to vehicles; and skill to replace, fit, install, and make adjustments. Experience demonstrating an understanding of the makeup and operation of the various individual systems maintained and their interrelationships. Experience reading and interpreting parts lists, manufactures' repair manuals, diagrams, and electrical schematics. SKILL AND KNOWLEDGE: -- Basic knowledge and understanding of the mechanical makeup, operation, and working relationships of individual systems, and their interrelationships for a variety of combat, tactical, commercial, automotive, special purpose vehicles and equipment. -- Working knowledge of various techniques for removing, adjusting, replacing, cleaning, and installing parts and components of combat, tactical, commercial, automotive, special purpose vehicles and equipment. -- Basic understanding of electrical, electronic, hydraulic, pneumatic, and other non-mechanical system theories; and skill to replace, fit, install, and adjust systems. -- Skill to use basic test equipment and ability to analyze test results to determine fault for repair or replacement of improperly functioning parts or components. Ability to use basic tools common to the occupation. -- Ability to determine when parts should be cleaned, reinstalled, or replaced with standard parts. -- Ability to read and interpret parts list, manufacturer's repair manuals, technical manuals, diagrams, engineering drawings, and schematics.
Education: SUBSTITUTION OF EDUCATION IS NOT CONSIDERED FOR WAGE GRADE POSITIONS.
Requirements: 
(1) Performs limited diagnosis, routine repairs and maintenance on heavy-duty mobile equipment, combat, tactical and automotive vehicles. Assists higher graded mechanics in the repair and/or overhaul of major systems to include internal combustion engines, turbine engines, automatic and non-automatic transmissions, heavy duty drive line systems, and hydraulic utility systems and controls. Makes routine repairs that can be accomplished by removing, adjusting, or replacing defective or worn parts and components. Performs work in accordance with technical manuals, lubrication orders, maintenance bulletins, regulations or management policies. (2) Performs limited diagnoses to determine the cause of mechanical failures by means of visual and auditory checks and/or uses basic test equipment such as compression testers, voltmeters, ohmmeters and pressure gauges. Determines when parts should be cleaned, adjusted or replaced with standard parts to complete work orders. (3) Removes, replaces, adjusts, cleans and installs parts and components such as wheel seals, switches, sensors, fuel pumps, water pumps, power steering pumps, brakes, filters, radiators, bearings, springs, shock absorbers, wheel cylinders, starter motors, mufflers, battery cables, and other items of similar complexity. (4) Independently performs routine repairs and maintenance functions in remote locations that can be accomplished by removing, cleaning, reinstalling, or replacing defective parts of components and systems using standard parts. Receives guidance and instruction from a higher graded mechanic or supervisor to perform non-routine and more complex repairs on portions of major assemblies and/or systems. May provide field maintenance at unit locations as part of a "contact team". Recovers and evacuates inoperable vehicles from the unit location of breakdown. (5) Conducts limited readiness and repair inspections on vehicles and associated equipment supported by the activity. Performs Preventive Maintenance Checks and Services (PMCS) and ensures vehicles and equipment are properly serviced, including brake adjustments, replacing hydraulic fluids, greasing, cleaning, etc. Performs other preventive maintenance operations as required to ensure that equipment is functioning properly. (6) May perform routine maintenance and limited repairs on basic communication equipment such as radios, field telephones, amplifiers, switchboards, recorders, intercoms by removing and replacing components and elements. Performs minor body and fender, or other metal repairs, using peening hammers, dollies and limited welding. Performs limited repairs and routine maintenance on small arms and accessory equipment by replacing worn or damaged parts. Makes minor repairs to canvas and leather items using bonding/sealing compounds and hand tools such as awls, canvas needles etc. (7) In conjunction with or in the absence of the Tools and Parts Attendant, may maintain supply documentation, and the receipt, store, issue, and inventory of tools and parts used in the trades operation. (8) Performs other duties as assigned.
Security clearance: Secret.

title: Executive Director, Supply Chain Management, G-3
text:
Your Resume must be 2 pages. If you submit a resume that exceeds the two-page limit, you will immediately be deemed ineligible for this position and will receive no further consideration. We recommend using a sans-serif font such as Lato, Calibri, Helvetica, Arial, Verdana, Open Sans, Source Sans Pro, Roboto, or Noto Sans, with 0.5-inch margins, 14-point titles, and 10-point body text. This is a Tier 1 position. The salary for Tier 1 positions in Army is normally between $199,172 and $209,600.
Qualifications: Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal Government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) and Mandatory Technical Qualifications (MTQ) related to this position within your resume. Your Resume must be 2 pages. If you submit a resume that exceeds the two-page limit, you will immediately be deemed ineligible for this position and will receive no further consideration. We recommend using a sans-serif font such as Lato, if available. Other acceptable options include Calibri, Helvetica, Arial, Verdana, Open Sans, Source Sans Pro, Roboto, or Noto Sans. Please use 0.5-inch margins. For formatting, consider using a 14-point font for titles and a 10-point font for the main body text. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of these qualifications, you may not receive consideration for the position. There is NO requirement to prepare a separate narrative statement specifically addressing the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or the Mandatory Technical Qualification (MTQ). MANDATORY TECHNICAL QUALIFICATION (MTQ): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that would satisfy the following mandatory technical qualification. MTQ: Knowledge of, and the ability to plan, develop, direct, integrate, and coordinate, the execution of depot and arsenal management, maintenance management, sustainment, materiel management, supply chain management, ammunition logistics, chemical and biological defense equipment, transportation, munitions programs, and management of the sustaining organic industrial base. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): In addition to the Mandatory Technical Qualification Requirements listed above, all new entrants into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the following five mandatory ECQs. If your 2-page resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and MTQ, you may not receive further consideration for the position. There are five ECQs: ECQ 1: Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding - This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4: Leading People - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5: Achieving Results - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program (SESCDP), or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you do not need to respond to the ECQs. Instead, you should attach proof (e.g., SF-50, Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB)) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES.
Education: FOREIGN EDUCATION: If you are using education completed in foreign colleges or universities to meet the qualification requirements, you must show the education credentials have been evaluated by a private organization that specializes in interpretation of foreign education programs and such education has been deemed equivalent to that gained in an accredited U.S. education program; or full credit has been given for the courses at a U.S. accredited college or university. For further information, visit: http://www.ed.gov/about/offices/list/ous/international/usnei/us/edlite-visitus-forrecog.html.
Requirements: CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT: Must be a U.S. Citizen. You will be required to provide proof of U.S. Citizenship. One year trial/probationary period may be required. You will serve a one-year probationary period unless you have previously completed the probationary period in the SES. Complete a Declaration for Federal Employment to determine your suitability for Federal employment, at the time requested by the agency If you are a male applicant born after December 31, 1959, certify that you have registered with the Selective Service System or are exempt from having to do so. You must be able to submit and pass designated and/or Random Drug Testing as required. File a Confidential Financial Disclosure Report OGE-278e within 30 days of appointment and annually from then on. title: CPS SENIOR HYPERSONICS RESIDENT ENGINEER
text:
This is a public notice flyer to notify interested applicants of anticipated vacancies. Applications will not be accepted through this flyer. Interested applicants must follow the directions in the "How to Apply" section of this flyer to be considered. There may or may not be actual vacancies filled from this flyer.
